experiment: Experiment 61 — Post-alignment OOF Reliability versus End-to-end Adaptive CADR Graph Propagation

optimization.best_checkpoint: strict ACC improvement under historical val=test protocol
optimization.relation_pair_candidate_priority: union of the four anchor GraphLearn candidate supports

cadr.conditioned_adversary: shared 4-way modality classifier over pair feature + same/different one-hot
cadr.corr_anchor: detach CORR only in adversarial branch; PHENO/ANAT/FUNC use GRL
cadr.edge_weight: original selected similarity * confidence * reliability * sigmoid(edge_gate)

groups.name: POSTALIGN_OOF
groups.after_warmup: one patient-disjoint 3-fold jointly aligned relation OOF; fixed reliability then CADR graph or exact original GraphLearn fallback

groups.name: E2E_ADAPTIVE_GATE
groups.after_warmup: no OOF or reliability; four learned sigmoid scalar gates initialized at .1 blend original graph and CADR disease messages

oof.reliability: valid iff AUC>=0.55 and mean_same_logit>mean_different_logit; clip((AUC-.5)/.25,0,1), else 0
oof.selection_epoch: fixed tenth epoch; no validation-based epoch selection
oof.calibration: none; OOF determines reliability only, never supplies main-model edge scores
oof.validation_labels_scope: pair AUC/PR-AUC and logit separation only

rng.oof_sampling_and_model_rng: local NumPy generators and isolated torch RNG scope

protocol_limits: Historical pre-CV preprocessing and 871-node transductive graph retained.
These are protocol-matched exploratory comparisons, not unbiased external generalization estimates.
E53.3 used its OOF-derived reliability and Platt parameters; E61 uniformly uses sigmoid(logit) without Platt calibration. The latter is a shared, predeclared difference from the historical base.
Conditional modality adversarial alignment is not a patient-pair CORR teacher consistency loss.
